title: Fast-fail surface: heuristic preflight engine for upgrade gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight heuristic preflight engine ("fast-fail surface") that runs immediately after a candidate runtime/model bundle is built. The engine produces a compact failure signature and risk score using cheap probes (static compatibility checks, small synthetic request traces, kernel/quantization checks, and KV-cache smoke patterns). The risk score decides whether to shortcut to full preflight pipelines (perf/eval suites) or fast-approve low-risk upgrades. Goals: reduce cost and time of validation runs, catch regressions that correlate with customer-facing SLOs early, and provide explainable signals for rollout gates across LTS and general channels.
acceptance_criteria: Fast-fail engine runs in under 3 minutes for 95% of builds and returns a canonical failure signature
Risk score correctly routes >= 90% of low-risk builds to bypass full perf/eval without missing high-impact regressions during the 4-week experiment
Generated signatures are stored in the release metadata and visible in the Console rollout UI
Integrates with existing rollout gates: can mark candidate for full preflight, can allow canary rollout, or trigger immediate rollback policy
test_plan: Unit tests for heuristic rules and signature canonicalization
Synthetic trace battery (10 short requests across prompt length buckets) to measure latency/kv-cache behaviour
A/B experiment: route 50% of nightly builds through heuristic + skip vs 50% through full preflight; compare false-negatives vs cost savings
Stress test the engine under concurrency (50 parallel builds) to validate resource isolation
Manual review of 20 sampled signatures against full-eval outputs to tune heuristics
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): run engine in shadow mode for all builds for 2 weeks, collect signals; do NOT skip full preflight
Phase 1 (selective skip): enable skip for internal nightly builds with risk_score <= 0.06 for 1 week
Phase 2 (customers behind feature flag): allow small customers to opt-in to faster upgrades behind a safety net; monitor for 2 weeks
Phase 3: promote to internal LTS patch pipeline with strict telemetry gating; require full perf-eval on any signature change
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff sync with runtime and SRE teams. Agreed scope: cheap probes only (no full model eval). Action: share probe list by 2026-03-02.

2026-03-02: Probe list finalized (static manifest checks, kernel/quantization detection, short sequence perf traces, kv-prefix cache behavior, dependency ABI checksum). Added ENG-31207 as dependency for prober infra.
2026-03-05: PoC engine implemented on a feature branch. Initial risk heuristic: weighted sum of probe anomalies + change in baseline latency > 6%. Early results: 72% of builds flagged as low-risk.
2026-03-08: Decision to store signature as a deterministic JSON string in release metadata. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7354

2026-03-10: Canaries in shadow mode running for 48 hours. Observed 1 false-negative where KV-cache miss pattern predicted low risk but full eval showed 8% higher tail latency. Triage notes added and heuristic adjusted to upweight KV miss signal. Assigned follow-up ENG-91359 for Sig tuning.
notes: Tradeoffs: the heuristic trades coverage for speed — some non-obvious regressions (model-internal quality regressions) will not be caught and still need full evals.
If fast-fail false-positive rate is high, it increases dev friction; we will expose an internal opt-out and tuning dashboard.
Future work: ML-based risk scorer using historical preflight and production incident data (Q3 goal).
